correctness.rationale: For each vertex of F_2(K_{r,t}), the token graph is bipartite between cross pairs and same-shore pairs. Open-neighbourhood domination forces independent conditions: at most one empty row/column in the chosen cross-incidence matrix, and edge coverage of an entire shore by selected same-shore pairs. Inclusion-exclusion gives T_{r,t}; deletion-criticality gives star forests for minimal cases, with unique treatment of one-edge components. Counting labelled stars via EGFs gives M_{r,t}. Explicit extreme configurations and exact Stirling counts prove the lower/upper formulas. The embedded verifier independently enumerates both half-selection families to K_{4,4} and full token graphs for smaller cases. Finite checks are corroboration only; the proof is uniform.

value.rationale: Natural exact total-domination invariants on the same standard two-token biclique families recently studied for ordinary domination are determined for all parameter values. The theorem supplies a full all-set polynomial and an exact inclusion-minimal set polynomial, classifies their spanning-star-forest structure, gives an exact minimum set multiplicity and a sharp upper total-domination number. The large gap between minimum and inclusion-minimal maximum (notably for r>=4) is structurally explained, not a small tabulation.
